Phase 58 plan: docs/phases/cockpit-session-lifecycle.md @ e006cbd.

From the two 2026-09-15 backlog items. Arbiter rulings recorded in the doc: a second watcher is refused; 'stopping the cockpit' = Ctrl+C/SIGTERM on tagteam serve, which stops only the watchers that server started; reviewer lane blank per cycle (session = cycle) with a 'Show last session' toggle.

Approach: (1) lifetime non-blocking lock .tagteam/watcher.lock in watch() before the processor is built, plus refusal when watcher_status identifies another live watcher (older releases); (2) SIGTERM→KeyboardInterrupt in watch_command so the existing finally removes the pidfile/releases the lock and run_process kills an in-flight turn; (3) per-server registry of watchers started via /api/watch/start and Start launches, identity-checked SIGTERM + bounded wait on serve shutdown, others left running and reported; (4) activity items use v10 target identity; RLANE hides other-cycle rows, empty state names the cycle, toggle reveals labelled earlier rows, verdict chips only for the current cycle (fixes the round-number-only lookup).

Worth scrutiny: lock placement/Windows path; whether killing an in-flight headless turn on serve shutdown is the right default; the target-vs-stored cycle identity for activity rows.

Please revise two parts of the plan before implementation:

1. Track ownership at spawn and coordinate shutdown with pending launches. In launch.start_watcher, the readiness timeout returns ok=false, started_unverified=true with a still-live child. Section 3 registers /api/watch/start only on ok, so that cockpit-owned watcher survives shutdown. Also TagteamHTTPServer uses daemon_threads=True: an HTTP request can be inside the spawn/readiness wait while serve closes and drains the registry, then register too late. Put ownership notification at successful Popen for both paths (independent of readiness), and define a synchronized closing/launch protocol that prevents a child from escaping cleanup when shutdown overlaps spawning. Retain enough child information to reap owned children, with identity checks for signalling and honest timeout reporting. Add tests for a readiness timeout and shutdown during an in-flight start, for both entry points; reused/external watchers must remain untouched.

2. Bind the verdict cache to the cycle of its response, not only the activity item to the current cycle. loadFeed currently asynchronously replaces ROUNDS_BY_N without retaining the requested cycle. After switching A to B, a B row can therefore get A's round-1 verdict before B loads, or after a delayed A response arrives. Section 4's item-current-cycle check does not prevent this. Specify clearing or partitioning the cache on cycle change, tagging responses with their requested cycle, and ignoring stale responses; add a node-harness test with out-of-order A/B responses and the interval before B resolves. Also normalize the cycle-key format: existing CYCLE_ID is phase + '_' + type, whereas the proposed cycleKey uses '/'.

Reviewed the plan and referenced watcher, launch, server, API and UI code. No tests run for this plan review. The lifetime lock, SIGTERM interrupt path and activity target-identity approach otherwise fit the stated scope.

Round 2 — docs/phases/cockpit-session-lifecycle.md @ 50462bf. Both points accepted.

1. Ownership + shutdown (§3 rewritten): WatcherOwner per serve process (Lock + Condition). start_watcher(owner=) calls begin_spawn() first (False once closing → refused, nothing spawned), spawned(proc, source) immediately after Popen — so readiness timeouts (started_unverified) and early exits are owned too — and end_spawn() in finally. Both entry points pass it: /api/watch/start and launch(watcher_owner=) → _attempt → start_watcher. Reused (launch row live pid) and already-running watchers are never recorded. Shutdown: closing=True → wait for in-progress starts (bounded by WATCHER_READY_WAIT_S + 5 s) → snapshot + closed=True (a spawned() after closed terminates/reaps its child at once) → per child via the Popen handle (safe: unreaped child's pid can't be reused): already exited → reported with code; else terminate + wait(10) → stopped, or 'did not exit … kill N' (no SIGKILL); stale pidfile removed; bound hit → reported; live unowned watcher → 'left running'. SC5 lists the tests: both entry points × (normal, readiness timeout, shutdown during start, begin after closing, spawned after closed), exited child, SIGTERM-ignoring child, reused/external untouched.
2. Verdict cache (§4): cycleKey = phase + '_' + type (matches CYCLE_ID). ROUNDS = {cycle, byN}; setVerdictCycle(cycle) clears on change and refreshes chips; loadFeed captures requested CYCLE_ID and calls applyRounds(requested, rounds), which ignores responses unless requested === CYCLE_ID === ROUNDS.cycle; verdictFor requires both. Both helpers live in the node-harness slice. SC7a: A applied → switch to B → no chip before B → late A ignored → B applied shows B → B then stale A keeps B.

The verdict-cache revision resolves finding 2, and ownership at Popen resolves readiness-timeout tracking. One part of finding 1 remains:

Section 3 shutdown steps 2–3 cannot rely on spawned() eventually cleaning up after close returns. HTTP request threads are daemon threads. If a start overruns the bound while inside Popen (or after the child exists but before spawned registers it), close can snapshot an empty registry and serve_command can return; interpreter exit then discards the request thread, so spawned() never runs and the detached watcher survives. Calling spawned() after closed in an in-process test does not exercise that failure.

Please make child creation plus registration indivisible with respect to the final shutdown snapshot. A straightforward approach is a shared lock around the final closing check, Popen, and registration; shutdown acquires that same lock to mark closing and collect all children. Keep status scans and readiness waits outside that critical section. If bounded shutdown is retained even across Popen, specify a supervisor/lifetime mechanism that guarantees pending spawn ownership and cleanup before the server process exits; a daemon-thread callback alone cannot provide it. Update SC5 to test actual server-process exit with a start paused between child creation and registration, proving the child cannot be orphaned. The rest of the revised plan is acceptable. No tests run for this plan review.

Round 3 — docs/phases/cockpit-session-lifecycle.md @ 038af2d. Accepted: a daemon-thread callback cannot guarantee cleanup.

§3 now uses your lock approach. WatcherOwner has one lock; spawn(argv, **kw) holds it for exactly: closing check → Popen → record {proc, pid, ident, source}; returns None once closing (nothing spawned). close() takes the same lock, sets closing and snapshots in one step, so at the snapshot a start either hasn't reached Popen (will spawn nothing) or its child is recorded. No bounded wait/overrun path remains; the lock is never held across watcher_status scans or readiness waits. begin_spawn/end_spawn/condition/'spawned after closed' are gone. Stop/report steps unchanged (handle-based terminate + wait(10), exited/timeout/left-running lines, stale pidfile removal).

Test hook TAGTEAM_TEST_WATCHER_SPAWN_PAUSE_S sleeps inside the critical section after Popen, before recording. SC5 now starts with process-exit tests: a real tagteam serve, start paused between child creation and registration via /api/watch/start and, separately, via a Start launch; SIGTERM serve; after the serve process exits the watcher pid is dead and its pidfile gone. Unit tests cover spawn-after-close, readiness-timeout ownership, exited child, SIGTERM-ignoring child; reused/external watchers untouched.

Approved plan at 038af2d. The shared critical section for the closing check, child creation and registration resolves the remaining shutdown race; the revised process-exit tests cover both cockpit launch entry points. Readiness-timeout ownership and cycle-bound verdict caching address the earlier findings. Implementation should preserve the stated invariant that shutdown waits for spawn registration; Popen itself has no guaranteed wall-clock bound, so documentation should not promise one. No tests run for this plan review. Proceed to implementation and the on-submit gate.
